lead: An open-source IaaS platform turns a rack of physical servers and their hypervisors into a private cloud. It gives users a web dashboard, an API, virtual machine images, networks and storage volumes, without a public-cloud bill. Eucalyptus copies the Amazon EC2 and S3 APIs, OpenStack splits the work across named services, and OpenNebula uses a small front end with hypervisor drivers. Indian campuses and companies use these platforms when data must stay on site or when a public cloud is too costly for steady workloads.
prereq: You need: service models from Unit 2 and hypervisors from Unit 3, plus the AWS building blocks in 5.5.

sections.h3: OpenStack: services that form one cloud

blocks.text: OpenStack is not one program. It is a collection of services that share an identity system and a message queue. Keystone authenticates users and issues tokens; every other service checks a token before acting. Nova manages virtual machines: it receives a request, picks a host, and asks the hypervisor to start the VM. Neutron supplies virtual networks, subnets, routers and security groups. Cinder gives block volumes that attach to one VM like a disk. Swift is an object store for files reached by HTTP, not a mounted disk. Glance stores VM images, and Horizon is the web dashboard.

Packages come from Linux distributions or deployment tools. A small install needs a database, a message queue, Keystone endpoints, and then the chosen services. You register images, define networks, create flavors, and launch instances.

blocks.where: H is the number of physical hosts; r is the number of hosts reserved for control-plane services; C is vCPU per host.
M is RAM per host in GB.

blocks.text: VMs = min(⌊usable vCPU ÷ vCPU per VM⌋, ⌊usable RAM ÷ RAM per VM⌋)
blocks.where: ⌊⌋ rounds down to a whole VM; min takes the smaller of the two limits.

blocks.text: Eucalyptus is an open-source private cloud that exposes Amazon-compatible APIs. A Cloud Controller (CLC) is the entry point and makes scheduling decisions. Walrus provides S3-compatible object storage. The Storage Controller (SC) manages EBS-like block volumes. A Cluster Controller (CC) manages a group of nodes and their network. A Node Controller (NC) runs on each physical host and controls the hypervisor, usually KVM or Xen. An optional VMware Broker connects to vSphere.

Because the API matches EC2 and S3, existing AWS tools and code can point at a Eucalyptus cloud by changing the endpoint URL. The match is at the API level; behaviour, supported features and limits can differ. Test before migrating.

items: Install CLC, Walrus, SC and CC on management hosts.
Install NC on every physical node.
Configure network ranges and register nodes and images.
Create user credentials and test EC2 and S3 calls.

sections.h3: OpenNebula, CloudStack and choosing a platform

blocks.text: OpenNebula uses a front end: a host with the oned daemon and a database. Sunstone is its web interface; the CLI and XML-RPC API do the same work. Drivers connect the front end to hypervisors such as KVM, Xen and VMware, to storage datastores, and to virtual networks. A host runs a small node package; the front end schedules VMs onto hosts. Images and templates define what to start.

Apache CloudStack is another open-source IaaS platform. It groups hosts into clusters and pods, offers a management UI and an API, and supports KVM, XenServer and VMware. It suits teams that want a simpler install and a single management server.

All four platforms need the same first decisions: hypervisor, network ranges, image storage, and user authentication. A test install can run on one host with nested virtualization; production spreads control-plane services over at least three hosts. Reserve control-plane capacity, because those hosts still consume CPU and RAM.

spec.title: Worked example: VM capacity
spec.aria: A flowchart of the worked example: 8 hosts with one reserved leave 7 usable hosts, 224 vCPU and 896 GB RAM; the 1:1 CPU limit is 56 VMs and the 2:1 limit is 112 VMs, with RAM capping both.

examples.question: A private cloud has 8 hosts. Each host has 32 vCPU and 128 GB RAM. Reserve 1 host for the control plane. Each VM needs 4 vCPU and 8 GB RAM. At 1:1 CPU overcommit, how many VMs fit? At 2:1 CPU overcommit? RAM is not overcommitted.
steps: At 1:1, CPU allows ⌊224 ÷ 4⌋ = 56 VMs. RAM allows ⌊896 ÷ 8⌋ = 112 VMs. The smaller limit is 56 VMs; CPU is the bottleneck.
At 2:1, virtual CPU capacity = 224 × 2 = 448 vCPU, so CPU allows ⌊448 ÷ 4⌋ = 112 VMs. RAM still allows 112 VMs. The smaller limit is 112 VMs.
examples.answer: At 1:1 the cloud fits 56 VMs; at 2:1 it fits 112 VMs.
examples.check:
def main():
    hosts = 8
    vcpu_per_host = 32
    ram_gb_per_host = 128
    reserved = 1
    vm_vcpu = 4
    vm_ram_gb = 8

    usable_hosts = hosts - reserved
    usable_vcpu = usable_hosts * vcpu_per_host
    usable_ram = usable_hosts * ram_gb_per_host

    vms_cpu_1 = usable_vcpu // vm_vcpu
    vms_ram = usable_ram // vm_ram_gb
    limit_1 = min(vms_cpu_1, vms_ram)

    virtual_vcpu_2 = usable_vcpu * 2
    vms_cpu_2 = virtual_vcpu_2 // vm_vcpu
    limit_2 = min(vms_cpu_2, vms_ram)

    print(usable_vcpu)
    print(usable_ram)
    print(limit_1)
    print(vms_cpu_2)
    print(limit_2)

main()

traps: OpenStack is not a hypervisor; Nova schedules VMs and calls the hypervisor.
Reserve control-plane hosts before dividing capacity; forgetting them overestimates VMs.
2:1 CPU overcommit doubles virtual CPU capacity, not RAM; RAM overcommit can swap or crash.
Eucalyptus or OpenStack API compatibility with AWS does not guarantee feature parity; test.
OpenNebula's front end is not the hypervisor; drivers and node packages do the work.

quiz.q: Name the OpenStack services for identity, VM images, and virtual networks.
quiz.a: Keystone for identity, Glance for VM images, and Neutron for virtual networks.

quiz.q: Why can an AWS SDK often be reused with Eucalyptus after changing the endpoint URL?
quiz.a: Eucalyptus exposes EC2 and S3 compatible APIs. The calls have the same shape, so the SDK's request format matches; the endpoint points it at the private cloud.

quiz.q: A private cloud has 6 hosts, each 16 vCPU and 64 GB RAM. Reserve 1 host. Each VM needs 2 vCPU and 4 GB RAM. At 1:1 CPU overcommit, how many VMs fit?
quiz.a: Usable hosts = 5. Usable vCPU = 5 × 16 = 80; CPU allows 80 ÷ 2 = 40 VMs. Usable RAM = 5 × 64 = 320 GB; RAM allows 320 ÷ 4 = 80 VMs. The limit is 40 VMs.

quiz.q: For the same 6-host cloud, what happens at 2:1 CPU overcommit, and which resource is the bottleneck?
quiz.a: Virtual CPU capacity = 80 × 2 = 160 vCPU; CPU allows 160 ÷ 2 = 80 VMs. RAM allows 80 VMs. Both limits are 80, so neither is a single bottleneck; RAM is now fully allocated at the answer.

quiz.q: Which OpenNebula daemon runs on the front end, and what is the web interface called?
quiz.a: The oned daemon runs on the front end; Sunstone is the web interface.

quiz.q: Why does a small OpenStack install need Keystone endpoints before Nova can start a VM?
quiz.a: Nova checks a Keystone token before acting. Without Keystone endpoints and a valid token, the request cannot be authenticated and Nova rejects it.

quiz.q: A team says, "OpenStack has an S3-compatible API, so all our AWS S3 code will work unchanged." Evaluate this claim.
quiz.a: Only basic S3 calls may work. Authentication, access control lists, versioning, multipart upload, consistency behaviour and error codes can differ. The team must test each operation and adapt the code where parity is missing.

beyond: Not for the exam. In industry, OpenStack is often deployed with containers and Kubernetes, and its bare-metal service Ironic provisions physical hosts. Search for "OpenStack Kolla-Ansible", "OpenNebula Sunstone", "Eucalyptus Euca2ools" and "Apache CloudStack". Newer work looks at edge clouds and hybrid clouds that place small OpenStack or OpenNebula sites near users. The same API pattern — identity, compute, network, storage — repeats in public clouds, so learning one platform helps with the others.
